subject.title: Feature: groupScope option to consolidate group sessions into main

question: Should an explicitly matched group or channel be allowed to share the agent’s main session, and should the first supported contract be per-binding only or also include a global groupScope default?
rationale: The choice adds a public configuration surface and intentionally permits group participants to influence context shared with DMs and other main-session interactions; source inspection cannot determine the acceptable product trust boundary.

options.title: Per-binding opt-in only
options.body: Allow an explicitly matched trusted group to join main, retain isolation everywhere else, and document the resulting context exposure.

options.title: Global plus per-binding scopes
options.body: Accept the linked PR’s broader contract, including a global option that can fold all group peers into main unless individually overridden.

options.title: Design named shared sessions first
options.body: Pause the main-session flag and resolve the broader configurable shared-session model in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/19929.

recommendation.title: Per-binding opt-in only
recommendation.body: Allow an explicitly matched trusted group to join main, retain isolation everywhere else, and document the resulting context exposure.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history shows the strongest cross-cutting involvement in routing, group behavior, and session documentation, making this the best available owner for the product and security-boundary choice.
